extension.description: Seren is a modular provider based, cloud service streaming software that is tightly interwoven with Trakt. Seren provides the freedom to view media from a single menu system from service providers of the users choosing. Please Note: This addon requires the use of a compatible cloud service.

Changelog 3.9.56 [FIX] MDBList - In Progress Episodes no longer lists an episode whose resume point is at 0% (a player that was only started, nothing watched). The two Merge - In Progress menus read the same MDBList data, so they drop those rows too. [ADD] MDBList - In Progress Shows (TV Shows menu, between In Progress Episodes and Next Up): every show you have started and not finished on MDBList, most recently watched first. A show is listed when it has an individually watched episode and an aired, non-special episode still unwatched (the same rule as MDBList - Next Up), or when it has an episode paused part-way above 0%. Shows on your MDBList dropped list and shows hidden from progress are left out. Like Next Up it stops after 30 shows, 40 recently watched shows examined or 25 seconds, whichever comes first. Changelog 3.9.55 [CHANGE] Fewer background launches. Every background task Seren starts is a fresh Kodi plugin process; on an Nvidia Shield that measured 4.6-8.5 seconds of start-up work each at Kodi start (about 1 second once quiet, a few milliseconds when the process is reused). At Kodi start the three start-up tasks (torrent cache cleanup, undesirables defaults, anime mapping updates) now run one after another in a single process instead of three, and in the 13-17 minute background cycle the orphaned-metadata cleanup and the local-timezone check share one process. The orphaned-metadata cleanup now runs at most once a day (it only has anything to do after something is removed from your library). [CHANGE] The calendars and the TV schedule no longer format every episode of every Simkl/MDBList-only show just to show one row (or one week) of it: the episode is chosen from the show's bare episode list first and only the chosen episodes are formatted. Replayed against the Shield's database the same episodes are chosen (0 differences across 30 fully formatted shows, every hide-watched/hide-specials setting, 69 weeks); the speed-up has not been timed. One difference is possible: an episode that Trakt has no air date for but TMDb or TVDB does is only dated once it has been opened, so it can appear one visit later. [FIX] A queued widget refresh waited for Kodi's home screen with no limit, which held one plugin process for 3-7 minutes at a time on the Shield. It now gives up after 2 minutes (the refresh is dropped; the next widget-affecting action queues a new one). This also applies to the refresh Seren queues when its settings change. [CHANGE] The Python library search order now looks in Python's own library and Seren's own folders before the other add-ons' library folders (the same change TMDb Helper 7.0.6 ships), which avoids listing every add-on's folder on first import on slow Android storage. The gain for Seren has not been measured yet. Changelog 3.9.54 [CHANGE] MDBList - Next Up now keeps looking for shows until it has 10 episodes to show (before: it only looked at your 10 most recently watched shows, so shows you had finished took up slots and fewer rows appeared). It checks up to 40 recently watched shows or 25 seconds, whichever comes first, and skips shows with nothing left to watch. Changelog 3.9.53 [FIX] MDBList - Next Up was empty for accounts like yours: MDBList sends a whole-show and a whole-season entry for every show with any watch history, and Seren read those as 'the whole show is watched', so no show ever had an unwatched episode left. Next Up now counts only the episodes you actually watched, so a show such as The Office (one episode watched) shows its next episode again. A show you marked fully watched on MDBList itself, with few individually recorded episodes, may now show an early episode as its next one. Changelog 3.9.52 [CHANGE] MDBList - Next Up is faster: for each show it now reads only the episode list (ids, season/episode numbers, air dates) to find the next unwatched episode, and loads full details only for the episode it shows. Before, every open formatted and re-saved all episodes of up to 10 shows (about 14 s on a Shield with everything cached). The episode chosen for each show is unchanged. Changelog 3.9.51 [NEW] Simkl - Next Up (TV Shows menu, right after Simkl - In Progress Episodes): the next episode for each show you are watching on Simkl, most recently watched first, up to 10 shows. It uses the next_to_watch value Seren already synced from Simkl and was never showing, reads only local data, and formats just the listed episodes. Shows whose next episode Simkl gives without a season (some anime entries, for example 'E2') are left out rather than guessed. Changelog 3.9.50 [CHANGE] OMDb lookups pause for 30 minutes after OMDb answers 401 (a rejected API key or an exhausted daily quota). Before, every item in a list build repeated the failing request: a Shield session logged 261 of them while opening Next Up. Changing the OMDb API key lifts the pause at once; the metadata cache hash is untouched. Changelog 3.9.49 [CHANGE] The leet (1337x) scraper is removed again (a4kScrapers 2.99.143): 1337xx.to now answers every request with a Cloudflare 403, so it returned nothing. Its Tier 6 entry and its entries in the seed-count lookup table (TRACKER_TO_SCRAPER) are gone, and the Tier 6 description now lists the current providers. Changelog 3.9.48 [CHANGE] Restored the 1337x / 1337x.to / leet entries in the seed-count lookup table (TRACKER_TO_SCRAPER): 3.9.47 removed them by mistake, the leet scraper is still installed. The TorrentGalaxy mapping added in 3.9.47 stays. Changelog 3.9.47 [CHANGE] The seed-count lookup table (TRACKER_TO_SCRAPER) no longer points 1337x / leet at the removed leet scraper (each lookup failed on a missing module and only logged a warning), and maps the TorrentGalaxy tracker name to the new torrentgalaxy scraper. Changelog 3.9.46 [CHANGE] Scraper tiers for four new a4kScrapers providers (a4kScrapers 2.99.142, ported from POV 6.10.20): TorrentFunk, TorrentGalaxy and Torlock run in Tier 6 (public trackers) and TorrentDownload in Tier 7. Without these entries a new provider defaults to Tier 7. Changelog 3.9.45 [CHANGE] Maintenance release: a code comment in the skip-segment handler still named the old TheIntroDB v3 API. No functional change. Changelog 3.9.44 [CHANGE] Skip intro / recap / credits lookups use TheIntroDB API v4; the v3 endpoint Seren used is frozen and deprecated. No visible change: the same segments are returned. Changelog 3.9.43 [NEW] The source select window shows how many sources the search returned ("Sources: 42") under the title, in the style of the season / year line, and "Sources: 12 / 42" while a filter hides some of them. Changelog 3.9.42 [NEW] My Watch List Calendar and the TV Shows calendar (renamed from TV Shows Weekly Calendar to TV Shows Daily Calendar, since it now shows one day at a time) are redesigned after TMDb Helper's calendars: one page with a header row per show and its episodes under it, each with its air time (now in your own time zone), date, a status (Aired / Today / Tomorrow / In N days / Watched), a green tick on episodes you have watched and a Premiere / New show badge. Select on a show lists its unwatched episodes (Back returns to the page); Select on an episode plays it. [NEW] The TV Shows calendar shows one day at a time instead of a 7-day grid: Left / Right or the < > buttons change the day, the Today button jumps back, and Left / Right also work on a day with no episodes. A week is fetched once and the days inside it are shown from that copy, so stepping through the days is instant. [FIX] Air times and days in the TV calendars were UTC: an evening episode in the Americas was filed under the next day with a morning time. Days, times and the Aired / Today status now use your local time, with the daylight-saving rules of the air date itself. [CHANGE] The calendars now list episodes you have already watched (with a tick) even when Hide Watched is on, so the tick can show; the Unwatched view of a show lists only its unwatched episodes. [FIX] Movie Calendar: a month with no movies no longer closes the window - it shows the message and Left / Right keep paging months. Changelog 3.9.41 [NEW] Lists of anime episodes (Next Up, Recent Episodes, ...) open faster when Tag Filler Episodes is on: the animefillerlist.com pages of all the shows in a list are now fetched together instead of one episode at a time, and are remembered for 24 hours (a show the site does not know is also remembered for 24 hours, a failed request for 10 minutes), so opening the list again does not download them again. [NEW] Trakt pages that are already cached are loaded in a lighter form (only the status, headers and data that Seren reads), so a list built from a cached Trakt page no longer has to load the full web-request library just to read it. Pages cached by the previous version keep working until they expire. Changelog 3.9.40 [NEW] The browse rows that had no description now have one: Debrid Services (Cache Assist History, the current transfers of each debrid service, Clear All Debrid Transfers, Clear All Debrid Cloud Files, Clear Non Active), the MDBList Discover rows (Top Lists, Search Lists, Lists by Username) and the genre Multi Select rows. Changelog 3.9.39 [FIX] The "Simkl Sync: ... synced" and "MDBList Sync: ... synced" pop-ups that appear after a background sync are no longer shown while a video is playing, so they can't show up in the middle of watching. The sync itself still runs; only the pop-up is skipped. Changelog 3.9.38 [NEW] Every category in the settings window (General, Themes, Metadata & Artwork, Watch Accounts, Debrid Accounts, Providers, Scraping, Sort & Filter, Playback, Search & Titles, Shortcuts, Advanced) now shows a short description at the bottom of the window when you highlight it in the left-hand list. Changelog 3.9.37 [FIX] Simkl marks a movie as unwatched as soon as it is set to Plan to Watch or Dropped, so Set Status now asks first when the movie is one you have watched; answering No changes nothing. The Cross-Service Sync also no longer copies a Trakt watchlist add of a movie you have already watched to Simkl as Plan to Watch, which had the same effect (the movie stayed watched on Trakt but lost its watched mark on Simkl). Shows keep their watch history when they change status and are not affected. Changelog 3.9.36 [FIX] On Simkl items, the Rate option is now only offered for a movie you have watched and a show that is already in your Simkl library. Rating anything else quietly added it to Simkl (an unwatched movie became Completed, which the Cross-Service Sync could then pass on to Trakt and MDBList as a watched movie); Clear Rating is unchanged. Set Status > Dropped now retries with the older Simkl name "notinteresting" if Simkl refuses "dropped", so it also works for a Simkl login that uses the older naming. Changelog 3.9.35 [FIX] The background Cross-Service Sync was meant to leave alone movies and shows you have set to Dropped on Simkl (a watched mark moves an item out of its status), but it only recognised the older status name "notinteresting" - Seren's own Simkl login reports "dropped" - so the protection never applied and a Dropped movie or show could be moved to Completed by a watched mark from Trakt or MDBList. It now recognises both names, so Dropped movies and shows are left alone. Changelog 3.9.33 [FIX] Seren no longer erases its MDBList login when Account Manager has renewed it in the background. Account Manager now renews the MDBList login a few days before it expires, and a Seren process that still held the previous login could try to refresh it, be refused, and wipe the whole login (including the API key). Seren now checks the saved login first and uses it when it is newer, and never clears a login that someone else rotated while its own refresh was in flight. Changelog 3.9.32 [FIX] The background Cross-Service Sync no longer re-sends, on every pass, the episodes MDBList reports it cannot match. MDBList names those episodes in its reply, so Seren now notes them once and moves on; the episodes that MDBList can match are unaffected, and the unmatched ones still sync to the other services. Changelog 3.9.31 [NEW] The background Cross-Service Sync (Settings > Watch Accounts > Enable Cross-Service Sync) now behaves exactly like the Trakt/MDBList/Simkl bridge in TMDb Helper. Watched episodes and watchlists now sync between all three services, not only watched movies (Simkl takes watchlist items as Plan to Watch and never has an item that is already in another status overwritten; anime episodes, specials and shows marked Not Interested on Simkl are left alone, and only episodes you actually recorded on Simkl are sent on to Trakt). Every service is now read live, and a service that cannot be read is skipped for that pass instead of being treated as empty, so a failed read can no longer cause your library to be re-sent to another service. Trakt and Simkl history pushes carry the original watch date, are limited per pass, and Simkl writes are spaced out to respect its rate limit. Overlapping passes are prevented. Changelog 3.9.30 [FIX] Offcloud was missing from Settings > Sorting > Sorting Configuration: the Debrid Provider row could only be set to Premiumize, Real-Debrid, AllDebrid, TorBox or Debrid-Link, and only five of the six priority slots were shown, even though the sorter and the settings spinners already supported Offcloud. Offcloud can now be picked for any debrid priority slot, and the sixth slot is shown. Also fixes the window failing to open when a priority slot had been set to Offcloud through the settings spinner. Changelog 3.9.29 [FIX] The TV calendar (My Shows > My Watch List Calendar) opened empty with an error when 'hide watched' or 'hide specials' removed one of the episodes it was about to show; it now just leaves those episodes out. [FIX] The Trakt watched-episode sync no longer stops with 'UNIQUE constraint failed: episodes.trakt_id' when Trakt renumbers a show's episodes (for example specials moving up by one) - the affected episodes are now updated to their new ids. [FIX] Trakt movie-calendar items no longer log a flood of 'Error detecting trakt item type' errors; they were handled correctly already. Changelog 3.9.28 [FIX] Housekeeping: Seren no longer calls Python's deprecated datetime.utcnow() (ten places - Trakt and MDBList sync, the calendars, release-date checks and metadata handling). Python, which Kodi 22 ships, has marked it for removal in a future version. The times Seren computes are exactly the same as before, so nothing changes in use. Changelog 3.9.27 [FIX] The 1337x (leet) scraper is back in Tier 6 (reliable public trackers) and 1337x results from other sources are mapped to it again for seed-count backfill. Note that 1337x sits behind a Cloudflare challenge, so it may return no results unless the a4kScrapers package can get past it. Changelog 3.9.26 [FIX] Skip Intro / Skip Credits lookups for TV episodes (TheIntroDB) were sent the episode's own TMDB/IMDb/TVDB id, but TheIntroDB wants the show's id together with the season and episode number, so the lookup found nothing (or could match a different show). Seren now sends the show's ids for episodes; movies are unchanged. Also, when TheIntroDB reports its request limit has been reached, Seren now ignores a zero 'reset in' value and backs off for the next reported time (or 5 minutes) instead of retrying immediately. Changelog 3.9.25 [NEW] Account Info screens for Trakt and Simkl, next to the existing one for MDBList (Settings > Watch Accounts, shown once you are signed in). Trakt shows your username, time zone, join date, private/VIP status and - when your profile is public - ratings given and movie/show/episode watch statistics (a private profile has none, so those rows are left out). Simkl shows your username, account ID and type, time zone and join date. All three Account Info buttons now sit directly above their Revoke button, and the settings window re-opens on the button after you close the popup. Changelog 3.9.24 [NEW] Seren now has an Account Info screen for MDBList (Settings > Watch Accounts > MDBList > Account Info, shown once you are signed in). It shows your plan, daily API request limit, how many requests you have used today, how many remain, and when the quota resets (midnight UTC, shown in your local time). MDBList limits every account to a daily number of requests; once it is used up, sync and list loading quietly stop until the reset, and this screen now tells you why. It also works when the daily limit is already reached. Changelog 3.9.23 [NEW] Seren now writes a warning to the Kodi log when AllDebrid marks an API endpoint as deprecated (AllDebrid adds a deprecated flag to the responses of endpoint versions it is retiring), once per endpoint. Nothing is deprecated for Seren today - magnet/status already uses the newer v4.1 - so this is only an early warning for a future change. Changelog 3.9.22 [FIX] The playback watchdog (the stall monitor used with auto-play) had the same problem 3.9.21 fixed for normal playback: the item it hands to Kodi carried no tmdb/imdb/tvdb ids because they were read from metadata already stripped of every *_id field. It now carries the same ids the list row has (the show's ids for episodes and seasons). Changelog 3.9.21 [FIX] The item Seren hands to Kodi when playback starts carried no tmdb/imdb/tvdb ids: the ids were read from metadata that had already been stripped of every *_id field, so the playing item ended up with an empty id list. It now carries the same ids the list row has (the show's ids for episodes and seasons), so addons and skins that read the playing item's ids (subtitle and scrobbler addons, VideoPlayer.UniqueID) can see them. Changelog 3.9.20 [CHANGE] Cast, ids, per-source ratings and the video-stream flag on list items and playback items are now set through Kodi's InfoTagVideo (Actor, setUniqueIDs, setRating, addVideoStream) instead of the ListItem.setCast, setUniqueIDs, setRating and addStreamInfo calls Kodi has deprecated and warns about on every item. What shows in lists, Info dialogs and the player is unchanged; Kodi 19 keeps the old calls, and a value Kodi rejects is logged and falls back to the old call instead of losing the item's metadata. Changelog 3.9.19 [CHANGE] Video metadata (title, plot, rating, genres, dates, runtime and so on) is now applied to list items and playback items through Kodi's InfoTagVideo setters instead of ListItem.setInfo(), which Kodi has deprecated and logs a warning for on every item. What shows in lists and the player is unchanged; Kodi 19, which has no setters, keeps using setInfo, and a value Kodi rejects is now logged and skipped instead of dropping that item's metadata. Changelog 3.9.18 [CHANGE] torrentdownload removed from Tier 7 - its site accepts the connection but never sends any data (it does not load in a normal browser either), so every scrape waited out its full time slice for nothing. Tier 7 is now kickass, magnetdl, showrss and torrentproject2. Changelog 3.9.17 [CHANGE] leet (1337x) removed from Tier 6 - every real 1337x domain now answers with a Cloudflare JavaScript challenge that the scrapers cannot pass, and the only reachable clone (1337xx.to) ignores most search words and returns unrelated torrents. 1337x listings still arrive through Knaben, Torrentio and the other aggregators. Tier 6 is now eztv, kickass2, piratebay and yts. Changelog 3.9.16 [CHANGE] torrentz2 removed from Tier 5 - its domain torrentz2.nz no longer resolves and the only live torrentz2.io is a Google-search front page with no torrent index, so nothing could be scraped. Tier 5 is now bitsearch, knaben and Torrents-CSV. Changelog 3.9.15 [NEW] Torrents-CSV joins Tier 5 (keyword scrapers) alongside torrentz2, whose torrentz2.nz domain no longer resolves - an open-source torrent index with a public JSON API, no Cloudflare, returns info hash, size and seeders directly. The provider file ships with a4kScrapers 2.99.130 (which also fixes DMM, kickass, kickass2, magnetdl and YTS). Changelog 3.9.14 [FIX] Anime scrapers refreshed for AnimeTosho's wind-down. animetosho.org stopped updating on 2026-05-09 and its feed/storage server shuts down this month, so AnimeTosho now searches animetosho.net ("Anime Tosho NEW", a live mirror with the same search and AniDB filtering) first and only falls back to animetosho.org if .net does not answer. [NEW] TsukiHime joins the anime tier (Tier 1) - a free anime release index with a public API and no key needed; it only runs for anime and reports no seeder counts, so seeds are filled in from other scrapers when the same release is found elsewhere. [CHANGE] AniRena removed from the anime tier, together with its optional API Key setting (Advanced > Optional API Keys) and the old tracker-name redirects that pointed AniDex/TokyoTosho/AniRena seed lookups at it. Pair with a4kScrapers 2.99.128. Changelog 3.9.13 [CHANGE] Trimmed the service's post-startup "wait for widgets to load" sleep from 30 seconds to 15, to offset the 30 seconds of task staggering 3.9.12 added just before it. The startup flag-protection step (which undoes any service Account Manager re-enabled against your settings) now runs about 15 seconds later than before all the staggering work rather than 30, while widget loads and Account Manager's own startup sync still have well over half a minute to finish first. Service-internal timing only; nothing user-facing changes. Changelog 3.9.12 [FIX] Completing the 3.9.10/3.9.11 staggering work: the background service also fired three of its startup tasks (torrent-cache cleanup, undesirables list, anime-mapping update) in the same instant when it first loads. Same pattern - with "reuse language invoker" on that is three plugin interpreters created at once, a deadlock risk against Kodi's interpreter lock. They now run on separate 15-second ticks like the rest of the service loop. Lower-risk than the earlier two sites (nothing is tearing down at first boot to collide with) but closed for consistency. No change when "reuse language invoker" is off. Changelog 3.9.11 [FIX] The System.OnWake handler (runs when the machine resumes from sleep) fired the maintenance task and the torrent-cache cleanup in the same instant - the same pattern 3.9.10 fixed in the main service loop. Maintenance is the SQLite-heavy one, so with "reuse language invoker" on, the two plugin interpreters being created at once could deadlock Kodi's interpreter lock and freeze every Seren screen until a force-close. Cleanup now runs on its own 15-second tick after maintenance, matching every other staggered task in that loop. No change when "reuse language invoker" is off. Changelog 3.9.10 [FIX] With Kodi's "reuse language invoker" setting on, Seren's background service fired all three provider activity syncs (Trakt, MDBList, Simkl) in the same instant every maintenance cycle. Under that setting each one spins up a fresh plugin interpreter, and creating three at once - on top of the maintenance interpreter still shutting down - could deadlock Kodi's interpreter lock, freezing every Seren screen until a force-close. The list menus that hold an interpreter longest (Watchlist especially) were the visible casualty. The three syncs are now spread across separate 15-second ticks, like every other task in that loop already was. No change when "reuse language invoker" is off. Changelog 3.9.9 [FIX] Revisiting a show or movie list screen (Watchlist, Collection, My Shows, etc.) with the same filters could render it completely empty on the second and later visits, with every item logged as missing its info. The short-term list cache added for "reuse language invoker" sessions was storing the exact same data Seren was about to display, but displaying a list also consumes part of that data to build the on-screen listing - so the cached copy got consumed right along with the first visit's display, leaving nothing usable for the next one. The cache now keeps its own separate copy, so a cached list stays intact no matter how many times it's shown. Changelog 3.9.8 [FIX] "Drop Shows" on the Trakt Watchlist screen (bulk-hide multiple shows at once) carried the same deadlock 3.9.6 and 3.9.7 fixed elsewhere: the screen refresh it triggered on the way back waits for Kodi's home screen, which can't happen while Seren is still on-screen waiting for that same call to finish. Once hit, only force-closing Kodi would recover - the shows were still dropped correctly, just the screen never returned. Fixed the same way as before: that extra refresh is removed; dropping now returns normally. Changelog 3.9.7 [FIX] "Restore Dropped Shows (Trakt)" carried the same deadlock 3.9.6 fixed on the MDBList side: the screen refresh it triggered on the way back waits for Kodi's home screen, which can't happen while Seren is still on-screen waiting for that same call to finish. It hadn't been reported because it's timing-dependent, but the code path is identical, so it's fixed the same way - that extra refresh is removed; restoring now returns normally. Changelog 3.9.6 [FIX] "Restore Dropped Shows (MDBList)" (new in 3.9.5) restored the show correctly but then hung on a loading spinner instead of returning to the list. The screen refresh it triggered on the way back waits for Kodi's home screen, which can't happen while Seren is still on-screen waiting for that same call to finish - a deadlock. That extra refresh wasn't needed to show the updated list anyway, so it's removed; restoring now returns normally. Changelog 3.9.5 [NEW] MDBList's Dropped Shows gained a per-item "Drop Show (MDBList)" context-menu action (a show must already be in your MDBList watch history to be dropped, matching Trakt's own Dropped behavior) and a "Restore Dropped Shows (MDBList)" bulk-restore action on the Dropped Shows screen - MDBList previously only supported browsing dropped shows, with no way to drop or restore one from within Seren. Changelog 3.9.4 [FIX] Turning on Kodi's "reuse language invoker" setting through Seren's own Settings toggle no longer resets to off the next time Seren updates. Every update still ships with it off by default, and turning it on always goes through the same Settings toggle as before - this only makes that choice survive an update instead of silently reverting until you noticed and turned it back on again. Changelog 3.9.3 [FIX] Switching to a different Simkl account left that account's cached list rows visible until Kodi restarted - Seren already cleared this short-term cache on a Trakt account switch, but the equivalent Simkl step never did. It now clears the same way. [FIX] A show or movie item that was missing its metadata (a rare local-database gap) crashed the entire list it appeared in instead of being skipped. That item is now dropped from the list and the rest of the list renders normally. [CHANGE] Hardening for the Trakt list short-term cache added in 3.9.2: its read/write/evict steps are now protected by a lock (only reachable with "reuse language invoker" on and more than 50 cached lists in one session), and its cache keys now also include which Trakt/Simkl/MDBList accounts are signed in, so a future account-switch path that forgets to clear this cache can't serve another account's rows. Changelog 3.9.2 [FIX] When Kodi's "reuse language invoker" setting is on (it is off by default; some users enable it for speed), Kodi keeps one Seren plugin process alive and reuses it between actions. Seren's settings-changed handler only runs in the background service process, so several values the plugin process computes once and caches - which debrid providers are enabled, the metadata language/artwork option bundle, and the Trakt list short-term cache - stayed on their old values after you changed those settings from Kodi's GUI, until Kodi was restarted. The plugin process now compares a counter the service increments on each settings save and clears the same caches itself when it moves, so GUI setting changes apply on the next action. No change when "reuse language invoker" is off, where each action already starts a fresh process. Changelog 3.9.1 [FIX] When Kodi's video library runs on MySQL (set via advancedsettings.xml) instead of the default local SQLite, Seren's clear-our-bookmarks step - run once while handling a playback resume point - left its MySQL connection open on exit and relied on Python's garbage collector to close it later. It now closes deterministically, the same way the SQLite path already did. No change for the default SQLite setup. Changelog 3.9.0 [FIX] The Local File Manager's "Local Downloads" browser read the Download location setting once when the addon first loaded, so changing that setting mid-session had no effect there until Kodi was restarted. It now reads the setting fresh each time the browser is opened. [FIX] The source-select window's modal loop now runs on a daemon thread. Scraping always closes that window when it finishes, so normal use is unchanged - this only stops an error path that skips the close from leaving the loop running and blocking Kodi from shutting down, in the same family as the 3.8.6/3.8.7 worker-pool fixes. [CHANGE] The parallel step that resolves each row's Trakt match in the Simkl, MDBList and Merge menus (In Progress Episodes / Shows and the status-bucket lists) now uses Seren's hardened worker pool - matching the 3.8.6/3.8.7 pools - and cancels any lookups still waiting in the queue once the 20-second batch deadline is hit, instead of letting them run on in the background. The 20-second limit and the exact row-to-result ordering are unchanged; this only affects lists with more than ten rows, where some lookups queue behind others. Changelog 3.8.12 [FIX] The "Toggle Re-Use Language Invoker" Settings action, hardened in 3.8.2 to only ever force the setting off as a safety guard against the hang described in 3.8.1/3.8.2, was left permanently unable to turn the setting back on: router.py's dispatch resolves routes through a dict lookup first, which matched this action to the always-off handler and returned before ever reaching an older flip-either-way code path further down, leaving that path unreachable. Changelog 3.8.10 [FIX] 3.8.9 added a loading indicator to the calendar windows' initial open, but if the window's data failed to load the indicator could stay stuck on screen indefinitely instead of closing automatically. Changelog 3.8.9 [FIX] None of the calendar windows (Movie Calendar, TV Shows Weekly Calendar, My Watch List Calendar) showed a loading indicator when first opened - only paging to the next week or month showed one. Changelog 3.8.7 [FIX] 3.8.6 closed the two Trakt-sync metadata worker pools behind the addon-hang bug but explicitly left several other separately-instantiated worker pools uncovered. This closes the remaining live ones: the four source-scraping pools and the torrent cache-check pool in source scraping, the cloud-inspection pool used when checking debrid-cached files, the Cache Assist background-download pool, the stream resolver's hoster-list pool, and a fifth Trakt-sync pool (show/season/episode metadata refresh) that 3.8.6's original scan of the codebase missed. The source-scraping pools needed different handling than 3.8.6's - they're deliberately allowed to keep running past a bounded grace-period timeout so a couple of slow scrapers don't hold up results for everyone, so closing them here signals a shutdown without blocking on that wait rather than doing a full blocking close. The Cache Assist pool's background-download worker runs on its own pool's thread, so it also uses a non-blocking signal rather than a blocking close, which would otherwise have that worker wait on itself. Download Manager's pool was checked and confirmed to never actually be used - nothing to fix there. Changelog 3.8.6 [FIX] A rare, intermittent hang could leave Kodi's addon process stuck indefinitely (kodi.log showing a "waiting on thread" entry with no further activity) after certain Trakt/MDBList/Simkl list-sync operations, sometimes outliving a Cancel and requiring a full Kodi restart. Root-caused via memory-dump forensics (py-spy and WinDbg/cdb both failed to attach to the wedged process) to Seren's own background worker-thread pools - used to parallelize TMDB/Fanart/OMDB metadata fetches during Trakt sync - never being deterministically shut down after use; they relied entirely on Python's garbage collector, whose timing is unpredictable, and Kodi's own addon-invoker layer can block waiting on a worker thread that outlives the sync call that spawned it. The two pools used by Trakt sync (one for general metadata fetches, one for season/episode "mill" fetches) are now explicitly closed as soon as each sync operation finishes using them, and transparently rebuild themselves if a later operation reuses the same pool - closing this defect on every currently-known code path that uses them. Other, separately-instantiated worker pools elsewhere in the addon (source scraping, Download Manager, Cache Assist, the stream resolver) were not part of this investigation and are not covered by this fix. Changelog 3.8.5 [FIX] 3.8.4 fixed this for the season-by-season episode browse (Browse Show - a season) but missed the flattened all-episodes view (used automatically when "Flatten episode lists" is enabled in General settings) - searching for or opening a fully-watched show could still return "We received no titles to build a list" and an empty list through that view, live-confirmed against a real fully-watched show, for the same reason: the flattened view's episode list didn't override the "Hide watched" setting either. Changelog 3.8.4 [FIX] Browsing a season's episodes could return "We received no titles to build a list" and show an empty list for shows/seasons that were fully watched, even though the episode data existed locally in the database - the season list already forces hide_watched=False so shows always list every season regardless of watched state, but the episode list didn't carry the same override, so it inherited the "Hide watched" setting's SQL filter and excluded every episode once none remained unwatched. Episode listing now matches the season list's existing behavior and always shows the full episode list regardless of the "Hide watched" setting.
Changelog 3.8.3 [FIX] After 3.8.2 forced "Reuse language invoker" off, the Settings display for it could still read "Enabled" if it was already off in the shipped addon.xml at the time - the setting was only being corrected as a side effect of actually rewriting addon.xml, so when there was nothing to rewrite, the stale saved value was left in place. The setting is now synced to match every time this runs, whether or not addon.xml itself needed a change.
Changelog 3.8.2 [FIX] Enabling "Reuse language invoker" (Kodi Settings or Seren's own "Toggle Language Invoker" action) hung every subsequent launch of the addon indefinitely, because it collides with Seren's background service's permanent keep-alive loop holding onto its own invoker slot. Changelog 3.7.6 [FIX] The in-addon Sort Select dialog's audio/subtitle-language sort option was reachable by cycling a priority level's method selector 10-11 times, but was never wired into settings or consumed by the source-sort logic - saving that selection could crash source sorting on every subsequent scrape. [FIX] Removed one unused blank language string and 7 language strings left over from the removed audio/subtitle-language sort option above, and fixed one missing blank-line separator between two language file entries. Changelog 3.7.5 [FIX] Reuselanguageinvoker preference was being silently force-disabled on every version change. do_version_change() read a bare "reuselanguageinvoker" setting key that settings.xml has never declared (only "reuselanguageinvoker.status" and "reuselanguageinvoker.toggle" exist), so the check always evaluated false regardless of what the user had actually saved. Changelog 3.7.4 [FIX] 3.7.3's revert of episode prefetch was itself wrong - it was based on checking only the season/episode browse screens (which genuinely never paginate) and missed that four other screens (On Deck, My Recent Episodes, My Upcoming Episodes, My Watched Episodes/History) build their episode lists through a different, separate code path that does paginate. Episode prefetch is restored and now correctly covers exactly those four screens. Season prefetch stays out - Seren has exactly one season-list screen and it genuinely never paginates (always shows every season at once), so there's still no next page for it to prefetch. Reverted the change; movie/show list prefetch (working as intended, unaffected) is unchanged. This was incomplete and wrongly reverted episode prefetch too - see 3.7.4. Changelog 3.7.2 [FIX] 3.7.1's fix for the startup "database is locked" cache-cleanup error only covered a cleanup thread's own pooled connection colliding with itself - live-testing showed the error still occurring afterward, isolated (by temporarily reverting to pre-3.7.0 connection handling and confirming the error disappeared) to a different, concurrently-running thread's own long-lived pooled connection to the same file, which no amount of evicting the current thread's connection can prevent. The fast-bulk cleanup/rebuild PRAGMAs (synchronous=OFF, journal_mode=MEMORY) require no other connection have the file open at all, and connections are now deliberately kept open for a thread's whole lifetime instead of closing after each query - so this exclusivity requirement can no longer be reliably guaranteed. Cleanup and rebuild now treat that PRAGMA flip as a best-effort speed optimization: if it fails because another connection has the file open, they log a warning and continue using the database's default (WAL) settings instead of crashing - correctness is unaffected either way, only the speed of that one maintenance pass. Changelog 3.7.1 [FIX] Live-testing 3.7.0's connection pooling surfaced a startup "database is locked" error in cache maintenance cleanup - pooled connections now stay open for a thread's lifetime instead of closing after each query, so a maintenance thread's own pooled connection could still be open when that same thread tried to flip journal mode for a bulk cleanup pass (an operation that requires no other connection to the file). Both cleanup paths now drop their own pooled connection first. This fix was incomplete - see 3.7.2. Changelog 3.7.0 [NEW] Database connections are now pooled per-thread instead of opened fresh on every query, cutting repeated connect/PRAGMA overhead across every SQLite-backed cache (Trakt/MDBList/Simkl sync, torrent/debrid cache, provider performance, etc.) - a Rebuild Database automatically invalidates the pool, and any connection that ever gets stuck self-heals on its next use. [NEW] Provider performance telemetry is now written once per scrape in a single batched database write instead of spawning a background write per provider, reducing write overhead during source scraping with no change to what's tracked or how auto-disable works. [NEW] Background next-page prefetching (populates the cache ahead of you paging forward) now also covers episode and season lists, previously movie/show lists only. Never actually took effect - see 3.7.3. Changelog 3.6.8 [NEW] Movie Calendar and TV Schedule now prefetch the adjacent month/week in the background as you browse - landing on a month or week fetches the next one 3 seconds later and the previous one 5 seconds after that, so paging to either neighbor is usually an instant cache hit instead of a live Trakt call. Re-triggered on every navigation, so the two periods kept warm always follow wherever you're currently browsing. A per-period lock prevents a background prefetch and a manual navigation to the same month/week from both fetching Trakt at the same time. Changelog 3.6.7 [NEW] Movie Calendar's poster grid now pages to the previous/next month with the Left/Right keys, not just by clicking the on-screen Prev/Next buttons - pressing Left at the leftmost column of any row (or Right at a row's last item, partial last row included) now pages the same way clicking those buttons already did. Changelog 3.6.6 [FIX] Movie Calendar could display the wrong release date for a movie once a month had already been viewed and cached - a separate, pre-existing part of Seren's shared metadata layer can independently recompute a movie's release date sometime after its original calendar fetch (its own per-country release-type selection, unrelated to Movie Calendar's own cache), and re-reading that shared field on every cache-hit re-render let the two drift apart: a movie correctly shown under its earliest release date on first fetch could later re-render under a substantially later date once the shared field had since changed underneath it. Movie Calendar's fetch-bookkeeping now persists the date it originally used to place a movie in a given month and reuses that exact date on every future cache hit, keeping its own bookkeeping decision and its own display permanently in sync. Scoped to Movie Calendar's display only - the shared release-date field itself (also used by Browse, Info dialogs, and elsewhere in Seren) is unaffected by this fix and can still show the later date for these same movies. Changelog 3.6.5 [NEW] Movie Calendar now caches its Trakt-sourced layer per month, matching TV Schedule's existing fetch-bookkeeping design - re-opening an already-viewed month re-hydrates from the local database instead of re-querying Trakt's calendar endpoint. Changelog 3.6.4 [FIX] My Watch List Calendar's Trakt layer only ran calendars/my/shows (Trakt's OAuth-only personal endpoint) when Trakt was linked, going completely empty on that side with Trakt off - unlike Movie Calendar/TV Schedule, whose own base layers hit Trakt's public calendars/all/* endpoint regardless of account linking. Trakt-off now falls back to the same public endpoint for the same combined recent+upcoming window, matching the other two calendars' floor coverage. Simkl/MDBList's own watchlist union layer was already independent of Trakt's state and is unaffected. [NEW] All three calendars (Movie Calendar, TV Schedule, My Watch List Calendar) now show Simkl's or MDBList's own rating for a show/movie that only appears because that service surfaced it, instead of always falling back to a Trakt/TMDB rating. Previously nothing in Seren blended either service's own score into these calendars - only the dedicated MDBList list-browsing screens touched that data. Scoped to the same capped Simkl plan-to-watch/MDBList watchlist union layer each calendar already resolves, not the full Trakt-sourced item set; MDBList's 0-100 score_average is normalized to the same 0-10 scale as Trakt/Simkl/TMDB before display. Changelog 3.6.3 [NEW] Movie Calendar now unions in movies from your Simkl plan-to-watch list and MDBList watchlist that Trakt's own calendar doesn't already cover, the same watchlist-layer union TV Schedule and the original Calendar already do for shows. Previously the MDBList/Simkl gate only controlled whether the menu was visible - the movie data itself was 100% Trakt's calendars/all/movies endpoint, so a watchlisted movie with no Trakt calendar listing never appeared. The write path now only bookkeeps episodes whose actual air date falls inside the requested week, matching the check the render path already enforced. Changelog 3.5.27 [FIX] The "Select shows to drop" (Trakt - Watchlist) and "Select shows to restore" (Trakt - Dropped Shows) multiselect dialogs showed each show title with a large empty gap around it, fitting only 3-4 titles on screen at once. Changelog 3.5.23 [CHANGE] Movie Calendar's poster badge no longer shows the day-of-month - it was redundant with the release-date label already shown at the bottom-left of every tile. Built as five mutually-exclusive height buckets rather than a true radial/clockwise wipe: Kodi's progress control has no vertical-fill mode (confirmed against the official control spec) and a real pie-wipe would need ~12 generated mask images per layout for a result that's still visibly stepped, not smooth - the bucket approach reuses the same white.png+colordiffuse tinting already used elsewhere on this tile and needed zero new image assets. Changelog 3.5.22 [FIX] Movie Calendar - three rendering defects found during live testing, all in movie_calendar.xml only, no data/logic changes: (1) the rating label used a 6-digit textcolor (FFD700) instead of 8-digit ARGB - Kodi parsed the missing alpha channel as 00 (fully transparent), so the rating number was computed correctly but invisible on every tile; now FFFFD700. Changelog 3.5.17 [FIX] Turning off the Easynews provider (Providers settings) also silently disabled any Orion-sourced "direct" category sources for the rest of the session. getSources.py's _create_direct_threads() unconditionally emptied the shared direct_providers list whenever the Easynews toggle was off, instead of removing only Easynews's own entries. Orion contributes to all four provider categories (torrent/hoster/adaptive/direct) and already has its own independent toggle that filters Orion out of each of the other three lists when Orion itself is off - Easynews's toggle wasn't following that same targeted-filter pattern for the fourth. Fixed by filtering direct_providers down to non-a4kNewsgroups entries instead of clearing the list outright, so Orion's direct sources (and any future direct-category provider pack) keep running independently of the Easynews setting. Confirmed via the live provider-package folder names (a4kNewsgroups, Orion) that the filter targets the correct package identifier. [FIX] Easynews streams had no protection against Kodi issuing seek/range requests against tokenised CDN URLs mid-playback. Two other Kodi addons that integrate Easynews (plugin.video.easynewsx, plugin.video.pov) both independently work around this by marking the stream non-seekable, and Seren's own playback watchdog only actively monitors the first ~30 seconds after a source starts - a seek failure later in playback wasn't covered by anything. a4kNewsgroups' easynews.py (provider package, updated alongside this release) can now append seekable=0 to the resolved stream URL, gated behind a new "Disable Seeking (Improves Reliability)" toggle in the a4kNewsgroups package's own settings (Manage Provider Packages - a4kNewsgroups - Configure). Off by default so normal scrubbing/seeking is unaffected unless explicitly enabled - turning it on trades seek/scrub ability for playback reliability on setups that hit range-request failures against Easynews's tokenised links.
Changelog 3.5.16 [FEATURE] "Rebuild Database" (Tools -> Sync Tools) is now unified across all connected services instead of Trakt-only - one click drops and recreates the local sync database for every configured service (Trakt, MDBList, Simkl) and forces a full re-sync of each, behind a single confirmation. MDBList and Simkl previously had no rebuild action anywhere. Mirrors how "Clear the last sync timestamp" and "Force a sync" already work across all three services; the Trakt-only action is unchanged and still reachable from Trakt's own settings page. [FIX] Rebuilding Trakt's database (and now MDBList's) could silently and permanently break "Add/Remove Custom List" and, for Trakt, Watchlist/Favorites menu gating for the rest of the Kodi session. Both features store their data in tables/columns added outside the normal schema specifically to avoid an unrelated auto-rebuild trigger, guarded by a one-time migration check that isn't aware a manual rebuild just dropped them - so after a rebuild, the guard skipped recreating them, and every subsequent read/write against that missing table or column failed quietly in the background. Fixed by clearing that guard as part of the rebuild, so the very next database use recreates them correctly. Simkl is unaffected - it has no such tables.
Changelog 3.5.15 [FIX] "Browse Show" (context menu) returned "No results found" for any fully-watched show, and resuming a fully-watched show with "Click Resume" enabled crashed with a KeyError instead of playing - both traced to the same cause. get_season_list()'s "Hide Watched Items" filter is meant for discovery listings (so finished shows don't clutter a browse-for-something-to-watch list), but it was also being applied when fetching a specific, already-selected show's season list for Browse Show and for SmartPlay's resume logic - so a show whose only or last season was fully watched had that season filtered out of its own season list, leaving nothing to browse or resume. Live-reproduced and confirmed via kodi.log (Star City, trakt_id 235622, 8/8 episodes watched: Browse Show returned an empty directory, and clicking to resume raised KeyError: 1 at smartPlay.py's get_resume_episode). Fixed by passing hide_watched=False at both call sites - the same hide_watched=False override get_season()/get_show() already apply when fetching one specific record directly (those two also override hide_unaired=False, which wasn't needed here since unaired episodes weren't part of the repro).
Changelog 3.5.14 [FEATURE] "Add to Custom List" and "Remove From Custom List" (Trakt and MDBList context menus) now reflect an item's real list membership instead of always showing both options unconditionally. "Remove From Custom List" is hidden whenever local sync data shows the item isn't in any of your lists - "Add to Custom List" always stays visible since its picker can also create a brand-new list. Membership is kept fresh two ways: immediately after you add/remove an item through Seren's own menu, and via a new periodic full sync of every list's contents (both Trakt and MDBList have no lighter-weight "what changed" signal for list items, so this walks each list in full - cost scales with list count x list size). Season/episode entries resolve to their parent show, matching how they're already added/removed today.
Changelog 3.5.13 [FIX] Simkl movie/show/anime sync could get stuck reporting an error every cycle for any account with a structurally empty bucket (e.g. no completed movies yet, or no anime at all) - Simkl returns a literal null body (HTTP 200) for an empty bucket rather than {}, which the sync code's failure check couldn't tell apart from a genuine request failure, so it aborted and retried indefinitely instead of recording "nothing new this cycle." Fixed for the three additive sync passes (movies, shows, anime) by adding a stricter request helper that raises on a real failure and lets a confirmed-empty response through as valid, empty data. The four removal-reconciliation passes (which use these same buckets to diff local vs remote state and delete stale rows) are deliberately left on the old conservative behaviour - trusting a null sub-fetch there risks wrongly deleting real locally-cached data once it's unioned with other buckets, so they still abort-and-retry rather than risk an incorrect deletion. [FIX] Trakt's "Remove From Custom List (Trakt)" context menu entry always showed "Item removed from {list}" even when Trakt's API silently did nothing, e.g. removing an item already absent from that list. Now checks the API's actual response before showing success, matching the existing pattern used by the Mark Watched/Unwatched entries.
Changelog 3.5.12 [FIX] MDBList "Next Up" could take upwards of a minute or more to load and could show a long-since-watched early-season episode as "next" for an actively-watched show. Two separate causes: (1) the feature capped itself at the general item.limit browse-page setting (default 20), and every one of those shows can trigger a one-time-per-show cold TMDb bootstrap of its entire episode catalog if never browsed elsewhere in Seren - now capped at 10 shows regardless of item.limit, bounding worst-case synchronous load time. (2) the "next unwatched episode" match compared MDBList's real season/episode numbers against get_episode_list()'s cached info blob, which can hold TMDb absolute numbering (e.g. season=1/number=48) instead of the show's real numbering for some shows - every real watched episode then silently failed to match, and the first episode in air order (usually season 1) won every time. Now matches against the same DB-authoritative season/number columns the episode list is already sorted by. [FIX] MDBList's watched-history sync now also reads the server's bulk-marked whole-show and whole-season watched entries, not just individually-tracked episodes - live-confirmed a second, often larger contributor to the "wrong next episode" symptom above: marking a whole show or season watched via MDBList's own site/app produces no per-episode record at all, so Next Up had nothing locally to treat as watched for that content and fell back to season 1 episode 1. A whole-season mark now credits every episode in that season; a whole-show mark credits every episode aired on or before the mark's own timestamp. One side effect worth knowing: a show that's entirely covered by a whole-show mark (fully aired and fully bulk-marked) now correctly disappears from Next Up instead of showing a stale wrong episode - there's no real gap left to report for it.

Changelog 3.5.8 [NEW] MDBList show/season context menu now shows only "Mark Watched" or "Mark Unwatched", closing the gap left open in 3.5.6 - compares MDBList's own local per-episode watched count against the episode count already loaded from Trakt's local data (used identically across all three scopes' menus), so no extra API calls are needed. Changelog 3.5.7 [FIX] Simkl's scrobbler (auto mark-watched at the end of playback) now writes the local sync database immediately, matching Trakt/MDBList's existing behavior - previously it only posted to Simkl's API, so the 3.5.6 context-menu toggle could keep showing "Mark Watched" for an item Simkl already had marked watched, until the next periodic sync. Shows increment the existing local episode count (clamped to the known total), since Simkl's local schema has no per-episode table - a rewatched episode can be double-counted until the next full sync reconciles it; accepted, since nothing currently reads per-episode Simkl state.

Changelog 3.4.14 [FIX] Movie list loads (Trending, Most Favorited, etc.) re-fetched full metadata from TMDB/Fanart/OMDB on every single visit, even for movies whose data hadn't changed since the last visit. Root cause was in the movie upsert's needs_update flag: once set, a nested SQL CASE expression had no path back to false, so every movie was permanently flagged as needing a re-fetch after its first save. Fixed the flag to clear correctly once a real metadata fetch completes, so repeat visits to an already-seen list only re-fetch items that actually changed. Measured effect on a test list: forced-refetch count on a 20-item repeat visit dropped from 20/20 to 0/20, cutting that list's load time from ~0.5-2.3s to ~0.18s. Movies only; shows/seasons/episodes were not touched (same-shaped code exists there but wasn't verified).
Changelog 3.4.13 [FIX] Settings navigation: closing "Playback Locale" always returned to the top of the settings dialog (General tab) instead of back to Playback where it was opened from. Root cause was a stale control-ID formula shared by every settings-return call in the addon - the underlying constants were wrong for every one of the addon's 12 settings categories, most of which happened to still land close enough to look right, masking the bug everywhere except Playback Locale. Corrected the shared formula and re-verified all 22 call sites against it (Playback Locale, Choose Sorting/Choose Filters, Download Location prompt, Theme color picker, and every Trakt/MDBList/Simkl/Real-Debrid/AllDebrid/TorBox/Debrid-Link/Offcloud/Premiumize authorize-and-revoke action) so each now returns focus to the correct row it was opened from.
